arcs.title: Dana: Haifa
arcs.stage: Tue Nov 24 night: she phoned after closing, 'one o'clock, I want to tell you myself, before someone does it worse'; he set an alarm 'Don't be late. Don't say sorry.' Wed Nov 25 (midpoint): the one o'clock talk at Cafe Nahat. Next: week 3 he stops going to the cafe.
arcs.secret: Dana has been offered a job running a new cafe in Haifa from January and must answer by Mon Dec 7. She has not told Ishai.

arcs.title: Gadi: Unpaid
arcs.stage: Tue Nov 24: 'Thursday payment run confirmed!!', P.S. the bank is 'slow in December'; at 13:41 he phoned to praise the free blue-and-silver banner. Next: Thursday's payment run; week 3 Gadi asks for January.
arcs.secret: Sababa Creative lost its biggest client in October. Gadi is paying every freelancer late and hides it behind cheerful 'small things'.

arcs.title: Noa: Shir
arcs.stage: Tue Nov 24: yes to Saturday dinner ('a ransom note with full stops'), 'Tomer talks too much', cut the call for 'nobody'; trivia with Tomer, second again (19/30). Wed Nov 25: Pump House with Ishai (engine); tonight she is the one holding him up, phone face down. Next: Sat Nov 28 he finds out.
arcs.secret: Noa's girlfriend of three years, Shir, moved out in October. Noa told nobody: it's why she is late, cancels plans and pushes Ishai's love life so hard.

arcs.title: Improv on Thursdays
arcs.stage: Lesson 3 Thu Nov 19. Lesson 4 Thu Nov 26, the last one Noa paid for, the day after the midpoint: where he first says out loud what he wants.

arcs.title: Mrs. Levi's cough
arcs.stage: Tue Nov 24: Ishai helped her send Eli the photo of Yitzhak with the candles: two grey ticks, 'he's very busy', honey cake; at 22:41 she was still checking the phone at her door. Wed Nov 25: Moti tells Ishai to ask her 'how long', tomorrow. Next: Thu Nov 26 she admits it (four years); week 3 Ishai quietly messages Eli.
arcs.secret: Mrs. Levi is lonely: her son Eli in Toronto hasn't visited in four years, and she always says he's busy.

arcs.title: Avi's kiosk
arcs.stage: Tue Nov 24: on the phone at the back all lunch; he came up at 16:51 for Ishai's Macaroni Pie and said nothing about the envelope. Next: the telling Thu Nov 26.
arcs.secret: Avi's landlord is doubling the kiosk's rent from January.

arcs.title: Lior's novel and Moshe
arcs.stage: Fri Nov 20: chapter fourteen, the barista and the streets up north. Wed Nov 25: at Cafe Nahat, sure Ishai already knows, he lets Haifa slip. Next: Sun Nov 29 Ishai reads chapter one.
arcs.secret: Lior's novel is about Ishai: 'the man who apologises to his coffee'.

arcs.title: Tomer and Noa
arcs.stage: Tue Nov 24: trivia with Noa and Ishai, then a late call: 'go to sleep, seven words aren't a novel'. Saturday he goes to the PixelPlex with Ishai (engine: A Midsummer Night's Dream). Next: showing up for Noa.
arcs.secret: Tomer has liked Noa since school.

arcs.title: Mr. Zelig's bench
arcs.stage: Mon Nov 23: 'the cold end of the wood'. Wed Nov 25: Ishai comes to the bench after the cafe. Next: he keeps the bench warm through week 3.

arcs.title: The poker table
arcs.stage: First night Mon Nov 23: first of five, 91 up. Tue Nov 24 at Avi's Ishai lent Yossi 200 (the 91 plus 109), 'don't tell Boaz'. Next: second night Mon Dec 7, Yossi pays back in coins.

beats.goal: Ishai comes out with Falafel for the morning walk, already checking the time for one o'clock. Moti (Apt 1, committee head, still sore from losing 100 at poker) is on the landing with his receipt book: building fees by Thursday, and the stair light Ishai still owes for. Ishai pays in coins and small notes. Moti notices he's distracted. Then, quieter, Moti asks if Eli answered Mrs. Levi's photo. 'Two grey ticks.' Moti says: ask her how long since Eli came. Not today, she's tired. Tomorrow. He won't say more; it's hers to tell. He must NOT say four years.
beats.teaser: Moti collects the fees, and drops a question about Mrs. Levi.
beats.forceText: On the landing Moti collects the building fees and the stair-light money, and tells Ishai to ask Mrs. Levi tomorrow how long since Eli visited.

forceLines.say: Ask her how long since he came. Tomorrow. Not today.

forceCommentary.say: Moti issued a receipt for a hint. The committee is thorough.
'Not today.' Everyone in this building has a schedule for secrets.

moments.text: On the landing Moti waits with his receipt book and a pen behind his ear. Falafel pulls toward the stairs; Ishai is checking the time on his phone.

lines.say: Apartment four. Fees by Thursday. And the stair light.
Morning, Moti. The stair light. Right.
Forty shekels. It's been dark since the twelfth.
It's been fine. I count the steps.
Everyone counts the steps. Pay the light.
Coins okay?
Coins are money. Slowly. I'm writing.
Twenty... thirty... thirty-eight...
You're short two. Like my Monday.
Still sore about Monday?
I called every bet. It's a philosophy.
Here. Two more. Forty.
Receipt. Committee rules. What's with your face?
Nothing. One o'clock. I have a... coffee.
A coffee with a face like that. Hm.
It's a big coffee.

commentary.say: He's paying for the stair light in coins. The light will come on one shekel at a time.
'A big coffee.' Moti, write that on the receipt.

then.text: Moti tears off the receipt and folds it twice before handing it over.

moments.text: Moti closes the book but doesn't go down. He glances at Mrs. Levi's door, where a cat bowl sits empty, and lowers his voice.

lines.say: Did he answer? Eli. The photo you sent.
Two grey ticks. Last night she was still checking.
Grey ticks. Of course.
She says he's very busy.
She says. Every year, she says.
Every year?
Ask her how long since he came.
How long? Moti, how long?
Not from me. It's hers.
Then why tell me to ask?
Because you sent the photo. She'll talk to you.
Today? I can knock now.
Not today. She's tired. Tomorrow.
Tomorrow. Okay. I'll fill the cat bowl.
Good. And fix your face before the big coffee.
It's fixed. This is my fixed face.

commentary.say: 'Every year, she says.' Moti just handed him a secret with a receipt.
He's going to fill the cat bowl. Ishai processes everything through small animals.

update.memory: Paid the stair light in coins, forty. Distracted about a 'big coffee' at one. I told him to ask Mrs. Levi tomorrow how long since Eli came.

beats.goal: MIDPOINT. Back from the lecture, Ishai comes to Cafe Nahat early for Dana's one o'clock. Dana is stuck in the back with a supplier, so he sits near Lior, who is writing. Lior, sure Dana has already told him (today's the day, he heard her), congratulates him in a roundabout way and lets it slip: 'so we'll need a new barista... Haifa's lucky'. Ishai goes very quiet. Dana comes out, sees his face and Lior's, and knows. Short and painful: yes, a cafe in Haifa from January, she must answer by December seventh, she hasn't decided, she wanted to tell him herself. He says congratulations, it's big, not bad, leaves money for a coffee he didn't drink and goes out onto the shops block. Hurt and quiet, not angry. He does not say what he wants.
beats.teaser: One o'clock at Cafe Nahat. Dana wanted to tell him herself.
beats.forceText: At Cafe Nahat, before Dana can tell him, Lior lets slip that Dana is moving to Haifa. Ishai congratulates her quietly and leaves.

forceLines.say: I wanted to tell you myself.

forceCommentary.say: Someone did it worse. It was Lior. It's always the novelist.
He left money for a coffee he didn't drink. That's Ishai's version of slamming a door.

moments.text: 12:40, twenty minutes early. Dana is in the back arguing with a supplier about milk crates. Ishai sits at the table next to Lior, who is typing with two fingers.

lines.say: Early. For you, that's a statement.
I had an alarm. 'Don't be late.'
Good alarm. Literary.
Where's Dana?
Milk crates. A war. She's winning.
She asked me to come at one.
I know. Today's the day.
You know?
Small cafe. Thin walls. Big phone calls.
She said it's big. Not bad.
Big. Yes. Brave, I'd say.
Brave how?
Chapter fifteen is about bravery. Sort of.
Is everything a chapter to you?
Everything. Even you. Especially you.
I'm not that interesting.
That's what makes it interesting.

commentary.say: 'Today's the day.' Lior's walls are thin. His tact is thinner.
Twenty minutes early. Babe, you came to a coffee like it's a flight.

then.text: Lior goes back to typing; Ishai turns his phone over and over on the table, watching the back door.

moments.text: Lior stops typing and leans over with a warm, sad smile, the way you congratulate someone at a farewell party.

lines.say: So. You'll visit her, I hope.
Visit who?
Dana. Up north. It's not far by train.
Up north?
Haifa. Her own cafe. From January.
Her own... from January.
So we'll need a new barista. Tragic for the foam.
Lior. She hasn't told me.
She... hasn't?
One o'clock. That's what one o'clock was.
Oh no. Oh, I'm a fool.
It's fine.
It isn't fine. I heard her. I thought—
It's fine. Really. Haifa's lucky.
Don't say that like a receipt.
How should I say it?
Not to me. To her.

commentary.say: There it is. 'So we'll need a new barista.' Lior, put the laptop down and walk into the sea.
Ishai just said 'it's fine' three times. That's a new personal record.

update.memory: I told Ishai about Haifa before Dana could. I thought he knew. He said 'Haifa's lucky' like a receipt. Chapter fifteen is ruined. I am a fool.

moments.text: Dana comes out of the back wiping her hands, sees Lior's face, then Ishai's, and stops. She takes off her apron and sits down across from Ishai.

lines.say: He told you.
He thought I knew.
I wanted to tell you myself. At one.
It's twelve fifty.
Ishai.
Haifa. Your own cafe. January.
They asked me. I have to answer by December seventh.
That's... big. Not bad. You said.
I haven't decided anything.
But you want it.
I want... a lot of things. That's the problem.
Congratulations. Really.
Don't do that. Don't be polite at me.
I'm not. I'm being... polite.
Say something real.
Moshe is better. Fewer aphids.
That's not what I meant.
I know.

commentary.say: 'Say something real.' And he gave her an aphid update. My heart is in pieces, people.
December seventh. Twelve days. Moshe has more of a plan than Ishai.

then.text: Neither of them says anything. The machine hisses; Lior pretends to read his own screen.

moments.text: Ishai leaves a coin on the table for the coffee he didn't drink and walks out. Dana follows him to the corner, apron in her hand, the traffic light ticking.

lines.say: You didn't drink it.
I left the money.
I don't want your money, Ishai.
I know. I'm... not good at this.
At what?
At big things that aren't bad.
Can we talk properly? When it's not this?
Sure. Of course. When you know.
That's not what I asked.
I have to walk Falafel.
Falafel was walked. I saw you this morning.
He likes two walks.
Okay. Go.
Dana... congratulations. I mean it.
I know you do. That's the worst part.

commentary.say: 'He likes two walks.' Falafel, you've been used as an excuse. Again.
He didn't say stay. He didn't say go. He said congratulations. Twice. Somebody hold me.

update.memory: Lior told Ishai about Haifa before I could. Ishai said congratulations twice, left money for a coffee he didn't drink and walked off. He didn't say what he wants.

beats.goal: Ishai takes Falafel to the park and sits on the cold end of Mr. Zelig's bench. Zelig, feeding pigeons and talking to them, asks how the barista talk went (Ishai promised to tell him). Ishai tells him in pieces: Haifa, from January, he found out from the wrong person. Zelig's strange, gentle wisdom: the news is the same news, only the telling was stolen; a pigeon that flies off still knows where the bread is; and don't decide for her by disappearing. Ishai doesn't take the advice yet.
beats.teaser: Ishai brings Mr. Zelig the news. The pigeons listen too.
beats.forceText: On the park bench Ishai tells Mr. Zelig about Dana and Haifa; Zelig tells him not to decide for her by disappearing.

forceLines.say: Don't decide for her by disappearing. Pigeons do that. You're not a pigeon.
I'm a little bit a pigeon.

forceCommentary.say: Mr. Zelig, the only man in Tel Aviv giving free therapy to birds and designers.
'You're not a pigeon.' Put it on a mug.

moments.text: Mid-afternoon, the pond grey under thin clouds. Ishai sits on the cold end of the bench, Falafel's chin on his shoe. Mr. Zelig scatters crumbs and talks to a pigeon with one white feather.

lines.say: You. The barista. You said you'd tell me.
Hi, Mr. Zelig. I did say that.
So? Bread or no bread?
She's been offered a cafe. In Haifa.
Haifa. Hills. Wind. Good bread, actually.
From January.
And she told you over a nice coffee.
No. Lior told me. The writer.
Ah. The wrong mouth.
She wanted to tell me herself. At one.
And at what time did you find out?
Twelve fifty.
Ten minutes. Ten minutes stolen. Not the news.
It's the same news either way.
Exactly. So why is your face a funeral?
Because the news is... Haifa.

commentary.say: 'Ten minutes stolen. Not the news.' Zelig, you beautiful pigeon prophet.
The pigeon with the white feather looks unconvinced. Me too.

then.text: They sit quietly. Zelig throws crumbs to the white-feathered pigeon only; the others complain.

moments.text: The pigeons scatter when a jogger passes, then land again by the same bench. Zelig points at them with a crust.

lines.say: Look. They fly off. They come back.
Because you have bread.
Because they know where the bread is.
Haifa has bread. You said.
Hm. I did say. Unfortunate.
What do I do, Mr. Zelig?
What did you say to her?
Congratulations. Twice.
And what did you mean?
...I don't know yet.
Find out before December. Pigeons don't wait.
She said she hasn't decided.
Then don't decide for her.
How would I decide for her?
By disappearing. Pigeons do that. You're not a pigeon.
I'm a little bit a pigeon.
Then be the one that comes back.

commentary.say: 'I'm a little bit a pigeon.' Self-knowledge. Finally.
'Be the one that comes back.' Ishai, write it on the alarm. Now.

update.memory: Ishai told me the barista may go to Haifa; he heard it from the wrong mouth. I told him not to decide for her by disappearing. He says he's a little bit a pigeon.

beats.goal: At home, Ishai is spraying Moshe's leaves with soapy water and talking to him when Noa phones about tonight's Pump House (gallery night, she's coming). He tells her about Haifa, flatly. Noa remembers she guessed Haifa on the promenade, then goes softer and too sharp at once: people leave, it's not always about you. He says maybe he'll skip the Pump House; she won't let him: she'll be at his door at half past seven. Something in her voice is off; he doesn't notice. She must not mention Shir.
beats.teaser: Noa calls about tonight, and hears the news first-hand.
beats.forceText: Noa phones; Ishai tells her about Dana and Haifa and says he might skip the Pump House. Noa won't let him: she'll pick him up at half past seven.

forceLines.say: Half past seven at your door. You're coming. Patient windows.

forceCommentary.say: Noa called it on the promenade two weeks ago. Haifa. The woman is a weather service.
He's misting a basil plant while discussing heartbreak. Multitasking.

moments.text: Ishai stands at the counter spraying Moshe's leaves with soapy water, phone on speaker against the sugar jar. Noa, slightly out of breath, calls from somewhere with traffic.

lines.say: Ishush. Tonight. Patient Windows. You ready?
Hi. I'm spraying Moshe.
Romantic. So? One o'clock? The big thing?
Haifa.
What?
She's been offered a cafe in Haifa. From January.
...I said Haifa. On the promenade. I said it!
You did. You win.
I don't want to win that. Sorry. Did she tell you?
Lior told me. Ten minutes before she could.
Lior. The novel guy. Of course.
She has till December seventh.
And you said?
Congratulations.
Ishush.
Twice.

commentary.say: Noa predicted Haifa two weeks ago. Somebody give her a radio show.
'Congratulations. Twice.' The man is consistent. I'll give him that.

then.text: He puts the spray bottle down and leans on the counter, looking at Moshe; on the line Noa is quiet for a while.

moments.text: Ishai sits on the arm of the armchair, Falafel's head on his knee. Noa's voice drops; somewhere behind her a phone buzzes and stops.

lines.say: Maybe I'll skip the Pump House.
No.
I'm not good company tonight.
You're never good company. That's why I like you.
Thanks.
Listen. People leave, Ishush.
She hasn't left.
Sometimes they do. And it's not about you.
That sounds like it's about someone.
It's about art. Patient windows. Very you.
Noa, are you okay?
I'm great. Half past seven at your door.
Your voice is weird.
My voice is outside. Wear the blue shirt.
It's a gallery. Nobody looks at shirts.
I look at shirts. Half past seven.

commentary.say: 'People leave, and it's not about you.' Noa, babe, who are we talking about?
He asked if she's okay. She said great. Nobody who's great says great like that.

update.memory: Ishai told me about Dana and Haifa. I said it first, on the promenade. He wanted to skip the Pump House; I'm getting him at half past seven. He asked if I'm okay.

beats.goal: After the Pump House gallery night (engine), Ishai and Noa walk back to Herzl Street; Avi's kiosk is shuttered. Noa tells him he's allowed to be hurt, not sorry, hurt. Her phone buzzes; she turns it face down and won't say who. She goes home (not sleeping over). Upstairs, alone, a text from Dana: she's sorry it came from Lior, she still wants to talk properly, Friday after the rush? He types 'Congratulations', deletes it, types 'Okay', deletes it, and leaves it unanswered, looking at Moshe. The hook: will he answer, or start disappearing?
beats.teaser: After the gallery, a text from Dana waits for an answer.
beats.forceText: Back home after the Pump House, Dana texts: she's sorry it came from Lior and wants to talk properly on Friday. Ishai types an answer, deletes it, and leaves it unanswered.

forceLines.say: 'Okay.' No. Delete. Moshe, I can't even ask her about you now.

forceCommentary.say: Typed, deleted, typed, deleted. That's the saddest dance on this show.
Read at 21:52. Unanswered. Moshe saw everything.

moments.text: Late on Herzl Street, Avi's kiosk shuttered and dark. Noa walks Ishai to his building door, hands in her coat pockets.

lines.say: You looked at one window for nine minutes.
It was a patient window.
You were the patient one. Sad patient.
I'm fine.
You're allowed to be hurt, you know.
I'm not hurt. I'm... recalibrating.
Not sorry. Not recalibrating. Hurt.
Okay. A little hurt.
Good. Progress. Yael would clap.
Yael would make me say it in a circle.
Tomorrow you'll say it in a circle.
Your phone's buzzing.
It does that.
You can answer it.
It's nobody. Go up. Sleep.
Stay? The couch is free.
Not tonight. Saturday. Dinner. No plumbers.

commentary.say: 'It's nobody.' Second night in a row nobody's calling Noa. Nobody's very persistent.
She told him he's allowed to be hurt. Noa, who's allowed to hurt for you?

then.text: Noa turns her phone face down in her pocket and walks off toward the bus stop without looking back.

update.memory: Walked Ishai home from the Pump House; told him he's allowed to be hurt. He offered the couch. Not tonight. Saturday dinner. Phone face down.

moments.text: Upstairs, Ishai is hanging his jacket when the phone lights up on the counter next to Moshe. He reads it standing, types, deletes, types, deletes.

message.say: I'm sorry it came from Lior. I wanted it to be me. I still want to talk properly. Friday, after the rush?

lines.say: 'Congratulations.' No. I said that already. Twice.
'Okay.' No. Delete. Moshe, I can't even ask her about you now.

commentary.say: Typed, deleted, typed, deleted. That's the saddest dance on this show.
Read at ten to ten. Unanswered. Moshe saw everything.

hook.text: Dana texts: sorry it came from Lior, can they talk properly Friday? He types, deletes, types, deletes. Will he answer, or start disappearing?

previously.text: Will she get there first? Dana phoned after closing: one o'clock, she wants to tell him herself. He set an alarm: 'Don't be late. Don't say sorry.' He barely slept.

hosts: Wednesday. One o'clock. Dana wants to tell him something herself. We'll be there.
He set an alarm for 12:45 and labelled it. 'Don't be late. Don't say sorry.' Brave alarm.
'Big. Not bad.' He's been chewing on those three words since nine last night.
He drank chamomile at eleven for a nervous stomach. The stomach was not consulted.
Lecture at eleven: Coober Pedy. A town that lives underground. Relatable for Ishai today.
Moti is on the landing with a receipt book. Nobody escapes the committee.
Forty shekels for the stair light. Paid in coins. The light will come on slowly.
Moshe the basil: fewer aphids, more drama in his life than he asked for.
Falafel doesn't know what one o'clock means. Falafel is living the dream.
Pump House tonight: Patient Windows. Noa's going with him. She calls it 'very him'.
Second at trivia again. HERZL HEADS: the bronze-medal soul of Herzl Street.
Yossi has 200 of Ishai's shekels and a very quiet cap.
Gadi says the bank is 'slow in December'. Banks are fast. Gadi is slow.
Mrs. Levi checked her phone at her door at eleven last night. Two grey ticks. Still.
Avi ate the Macaroni Pie and said nothing about the envelope. Tomorrow, he says. Always tomorrow.
Twelve days until December seventh. Don't ask why we're counting. We just are.
Tomer's going to the PixelPlex with him Saturday. A Midsummer Night's Dream. Love and confusion. Perfect.
Ishai's coffee order is the same every day. His face today is not.
Rule of the show: the quieter Ishai gets, the louder we get.
Cafe Nahat has thin walls. Remember that. We're just saying.
Mr. Zelig's pigeons have heard more of Ishai's love life than his mother.
Noa says 'great' a lot lately. Great. Great great.
If he says 'it's fine' one more time, Oren drinks. Oren doesn't drink. Oren will start.
Tomorrow: improv lesson four, the last one Noa paid for. Big week for saying things.
Somewhere in Tel Aviv a basil plant is the most emotionally stable resident of apartment four.
Sivan beat her own record this morning. Nobody clapped. She prefers it that way.
radio: Radio Herzl 88.2, Wednesday, half the week gone and the other half already late.
Clouds in the afternoon, nothing dramatic. Unlike some people's lunch plans.
A listener asks: is it rude to arrive twenty minutes early? Only to your own nerves.
Next, a song about trains going north. No, we didn't plan that.
Traffic on Herzl Street: a delivery scooter and a man counting coins. Normal.
The building committees of Tel Aviv remind you: fees by Thursday. They always remind you.
Boolify says: true. Boolify says: false. Boolify won't elaborate. Neither will we.
Coming up, an old ballad for anyone waiting for one o'clock.
Wednesday night is gallery night at the Pump House across the park. Look at windows. Patiently.
Seventeen degrees tonight, a good night for a jacket and a long walk home.
Here's one for the people who said congratulations and meant something else.
Weather from the north: wind over the hills. Just the weather. Just saying.

zelig: The pigeon with the white feather never shares. Neither do I.
Ten minutes is a long time to a pigeon. Short to a man.
Bread in the north, bread in the south. Bread is bread.
The bench is cold on this end. He'll sit there anyway.
michal: Wednesday. Arms. And legs. And everything.
Run club Friday. Seven. I'm definitely coming this time.
The dog guy isn't here. Nervous day, I bet.
sivan: Nobody on the next treadmill. Good. Fewer apologies.
Speed eleven. I'm not angry. I'm fast.
lior: Chapter fifteen: the barista packs a box. Or does she?
Small cafe. Thin walls. Big phone calls. Good sentence.
Two fingers, three hundred pages. Slowly, slowly.
I should stop listening. I never stop listening.
He comes in at the same time every day. Today he'll be early.
kobi: Wednesday is a lottery day. All days are lottery days.
Number seven came twice. Twice is a sign.
The quiet one isn't here. Pump House night. Culture.
Another one? Okay. One. Then the system.

street: ...she said north, I said how north...
...forty shekels for a light bulb, can you believe...
...the falafel guy's quiet lately, isn't he...
...take the jacket, it'll be cold by the sea...
market: ...the cheddar's sharp today, sharp like my sister...
...two for ten, two for ten, last ones...
...he wanted mustard, I gave him mustard...
park: ...the old man talks to the pigeons, they answer, I swear...
...the duck has a name? Since when...
...three laps, then we stop, I promise...
cafe: ...oat milk is not milk, it's an opinion...
...is the writer here every day? Every day...
...the barista's in the back, she'll be a minute...

chat.say: Moti collecting fees today on each floor. Have small change. Receipts for everything.
Paid. Stair light too. Sorry it was all coins.
Coins are money. Thank you apt 4. Light comes on Friday.
Who left a cat bowl on the second floor? It's empty and the cats are complaining.
It's mine. Ishai fills it. Don't touch.
88 bus running late on Herzl, if anyone is waiting. Not my fault. Traffic.
Who has a charger for an old phone? Mine says 3 percent and I'm waiting for a message.
I'll bring one. Don't wait at the door in the cold, Shoshana.
The stair light is still off. Just so the committee knows.
